This is a well-specified problem with a clear, single correct answer — a math word problem with defined completion criteria, not open-ended generative work. That profile aligns with Avocet's documented strengths in retrieval/extraction-style, clearly-specified tasks.

That said, the routing-relevant capability signals here are essentially ties: the two models' relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval) differ by margins at or near run-to-run variance, so neither has a meaningful quality edge on this kind of reasoning task. Avocet's self-reported task preferences also don't predict output quality (the documentation explicitly notes preference is dissociated from capability), so preference wasn't a quality consideration either.

Given roughly equal expected quality, I picked the model whose documented task family most closely matches this query's structure (clear completion criteria), which points to Avocet.
